platform.windows: compiles; the Windows session path is T6 and no Windows QUIC run has been recorded
platform.note: The masque peer is a loopback HTTP/3 server on macOS arm64. Nothing is claimed for a platform that was not run.

pinnedImplementation.transport: transport/masque/masque.go (224 lines) + transport/masque/client_h2.go (325 lines) + transport/masque/l4proxy.go (137 lines)
dependencies: github.com/metacubex/connect-ip-go (CONNECT-IP client; vendored modifications for Cloudflare's non-RFC-compliant behaviour)
github.com/metacubex/http (HTTP/2 extended CONNECT for the h2 mode)
github.com/metacubex/mipstack or gVisor (userspace IP stack, IPStackOption)
pinnedImplementation.shape: Cloudflare WARP client: base64 ECDSA private key -> generated client certificate; public key pins the endpoint certificate; SNI defaults to consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com and URI to https://cloudflareaccess.com; `:protocol cf-connect-ip`; ADDRESS_ASSIGN/ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules; TCP/UDP are served by the internal IP stack. `network: h2` is an HTTP/2 CONNECT-IP variant and `network: h3-l4proxy` an L4 client; neither has a CONNECT-UDP path.
whyNotPorted: no h3 / connect-ip / IP-stack crate is in the offline cargo cache
generating the WARP client certificate and pinning the endpoint key cannot be exercised without an internet-accessible WARP registration
terminating TCP over CONNECT-IP needs a userspace IP stack; T6/T7 own device/TUN but not an in-process TCP/IP stack
the pinned adapter has no `listeners:` mode, so the pinned binary cannot act as a masque peer

implementedSubset.protocol: RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP over HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) with the capsule protocol (RFC 9297) and extended CONNECT (RFC 9220)
wireBehaviour: one QUIC connection per UDP association, ALPN h3, keep-alive 30 s, T10's capped transport windows
HTTP/3 client control stream SETTINGS with SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL (0x08); the peer's control stream SETTINGS is read and required to advertise it

one request stream per destination: :method CONNECT, :protocol connect-udp, :scheme https, :authority <proxy authority>, :path /.well-known/masque/udp/<target_host>/<target_port>/, capsule-protocol: ?1, empty user-agent
target_host keeps DNS/IPv4 literals and percent-encodes an IPv6 literal's colons (RFC 9298 §3); :authority is the proxy's authority (RFC 9298 §3.4)
2xx response with Capsule-Protocol: ?1 required; capsules run in HTTP/3 DATA frames; DATAGRAM capsules (type 0x00) carry context ID 0 then the UDP payload
unknown capsule types are ignored (RFC 9297 §3.3); a non-zero context ID, truncated capsule or oversized capsule closes that flow only

at most 32 destinations per association (MAX_CONCURRENT_DESTINATIONS); a closed flow (peer FIN, malformed capsule, oversized frame, writer failure) is marked dead by the reader task and pruned before the cap is checked, and reopened on the next datagram to the same destination
rejectedAtLoad: private-key / public-key (WARP endpoint pinning and client certificate)
ip / ipv6 / mtu / ip-stack / remote-dns-resolve / dns (CONNECT-IP/IP stack)
dialer-proxy (a QUIC endpoint is dialled locally; the socks5 hop cannot carry it)
rejectedAtDial: TCP through masque: CONNECT-IP (RFC 9484) plus a userspace IP stack is not implemented; the dial fails with that reason (inbound 502), it never falls back to DIRECT
notImplemented: HTTP Datagram (QUIC datagram frame) transport; capsules only
DATA frames larger than one maximal capsule (~64 KiB) are refused (local bound)
more than 32 concurrent destinations per association (local bound)

transitive: in-tree minimal HTTP/3 + QPACK codec (src/outbound/h3.rs); no h3/h3-quinn crate is cached
quicDependencyProfile.features: default-features = false, runtime-tokio + rustls-ring + log (the same profile as T10)
quicDependencyProfile.offlineSource: ~/.cargo/registry/cache; no network access was used to build or test
notCached: h3 / h3-quinn / hpack crates: the in-tree client is extended with server SETTINGS, request-stream opening and a frame reader
connect-ip-go / mipstack / gVisor equivalents: no CONNECT-IP client or userspace IP stack
uritemplate: not needed (the RFC 9298 default template is the only one implemented)
quicDependencyProfile.memory: Per UDP association: one UDP Endpoint and one QUIC Connection with T10's caps (stream receive window 512 KiB, connection receive 2 MiB, send window 2 MiB), the HTTP/3 control/QPACK send streams, the retained peer control/QPACK streams, and at most 32 bidirectional request streams (MAX_CONCURRENT_DESTINATIONS). App-level buffers are bounded per flow: an outbound queue of FLOW_QUEUE (2) x 65,535 B = 131,070 B; an inbound capsule buffer of MAX_CAPSULE (65,543 B) + MAX_DATA_FRAME (65,559 B) = 131,102 B; while a maximal capsule is parsed, the predecessor DATA frame (65,559 B), the capsule value (65,543 B) and the payload copy (65,535 B) can coexist, so one flow peaks at about 459 KB. 32 flows peak at about 14.7 MB, plus the shared inbound queue (2 x 65,535 B) and QUIC's 2 MiB receive + 2 MiB send windows. Approximate worst case for one association: 19 MB decimal (<20 MB), excluding allocator overhead and the rest of the iOS extension. The engine creates one association per SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE session and Limits.max_sessions defaults to 256: T7/T6 must cap concurrent masque associations (or lower max_sessions) to keep the whole extension within 40,000,000 bytes; this file records the per-association bounds, not a device measurement. No pool, no HTTP Datagram buffers (datagrams are not advertised).

configAndCli: crates/billow-kernel-cli/tests/family_cli.rs::cli_process_tunnels_udp_through_masque (successful SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE through the real billow-kernel process and a controlled HTTP/3 peer)
defaultSuite.harness: the CLI harnesses no longer take kernel ports from the OS ephemeral range: cli.rs and family_cli.rs allocate 24000-31999 (outside macOS/Linux ephemeral ranges, so a peer's bind(0) cannot steal a just-released port), probe readiness with the SOCKS5 method negotiation, detect an early kernel exit with its stderr, and retry a refused connect for 3 s. Five consecutive full-suite runs after the change were green; the earlier 1-in-5 ConnectionRefused at cli_process_tunnels_through_ssr was a harness port race, not a protocol failure.

controlledPeer.what: a quinn HTTP/3 server with an independent QPACK/capsule codec; SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL; 200 + capsule-protocol ?1 and DATAGRAM echo, or 403 / no extended CONNECT / no capsule protocol; CloseAfterEcho and CloseAfter(delay) modes for dead-flow reclamation
controlledPeer.whyNotPinnedMihomo: the pinned masque adapter is a client for Cloudflare WARP with no `listeners:` mode; an offline WARP endpoint does not exist, so no pinned-binary interop is claimed

optionMatrix.result: 204 no-op / 241 enabled cases, 0 problems; the matrix now prints `# skipped: masque (...)` because the pinned base requires the CONNECT-IP registration keys this kernel rejects

decisionsForT9: The T14 recipe was narrowed to the RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset; CONNECT-IP, the IP stack and the pinned Cloudflare WARP config shape are T18 (depends on T14). T14's subset is real but partial: a WARP-style masque configuration (private-key/public-key/uri/ip/ipv6/mtu/ip-stack/dns) is rejected by name until T18, so T9 must not count masque as compatible.

If T9 needs the pinned shape, the dependency decision is T18's CONNECT-IP client + userspace IP stack (pinned reference: metacubex/connect-ip-go + metacubex/mipstack or gVisor); no such crate is available offline.
The CONNECT-UDP subset shares the HTTP/3 client in src/outbound/h3.rs with Hysteria2; T18 should extend the same control-stream/settings surface rather than adding a second HTTP/3 implementation.
decisionsForT7: The per-association worst case is recorded in quicDependencyProfile.memory (~19 MB decimal: 32 destination flows, 2-slot queues, one-datagram capsule/frame caps, plus T10's QUIC windows). T7 must measure the extension RSS and cap concurrent masque associations (one per SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE; Limits.max_sessions defaults to 256); a dropped association closes its QUIC connection in MasqueUdp::drop and its flow tasks end with it.
iOS Network Extension builds link quinn/rustls the same way as T10; no extra C dependency was added.
